_comment: Real third-party repositories, pinned by SHA, scanned as a customer would.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-09-04 the known-good corpus gate was green
while every real repo it had never seen was BLOCKED: express 2, flask 2,
fastify 6, got 20, zod 51, hono 55. The corpus that was supposed to
guarantee precision contained two synthetic fixtures. A rule tuned against
this repo looks clean against this repo; that is the one measurement it
maxBlocking is a CEILING, not a target. It ratchets DOWN as precision
improves and must never be raised to make a build pass — raising it is how
you go back to shipping a gate that blocks express. If a change genuinely
makes a repo noisier, that is the finding.
minBlocking guards the other half. A scanner that reports nothing passes
every precision test ever written, so NodeGoat (OWASP's deliberately
vulnerable app) must keep FAILING. Precision without recall is a tool that

repos.name: express
repos.why: the most-depended-on Node package there is; the canonical clean control

repos.name: flask
repos.why: Python — proves the non-JS rules are held to the same bar

repos.name: fastify
repos.why: large plugin-oriented server; exercises the auth and route grammars

repos.name: got
repos.why: TypeScript HTTP client with a benchmark/ tree — a known scope trap

repos.name: hono
repos.why: every crossFileTaint finding here was false: c.req.query() read as SQL, RegExp.exec() as command exec; 2026-09-05 importCycle type-only elision: the four import cycles it blocked on read every binding inside function bodies — deferred, now a warning — ceiling ratchets down

repos.name: zod
repos.why: monorepo with a docs site and benchmarks; was the worst case at 50, of which 33 were errorSwallow — 23 in benchmark harnesses, 7 the parsing library's coerce-then-check idiom (2026-09-04)

repos.name: django
repos.why: Python at scale — the ORM builds SQL by string in django/db, which is the one place that is the job; 74 of 76 "secrets" were test fixtures before the identifier-keyed rules learned about test paths

repos.name: rails
repos.why: Ruby at scale — instance_eval in the routes loader, backtick-quoted words in error messages that a naive shell-interp rule read as commands

repos.name: spring-petclinic
repos.why: Java + Thymeleaf templates + a k8s manifest; the reference Spring app

repos.name: gin
repos.why: Go — the ignored-error idiom the go module could not see until 2026-09-04

repos.name: axum
repos.why: Rust — first contact 28 blocking: todo!()/unimplemented!() inside #[cfg(test)] modules, dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable read as a branch pin; what remains is third-party actions on @master and one real unimplemented!()

repos.name: laravel
repos.why: PHP — first contact 28 blocking, 23 of them `$redis->eval($lua)` read as PHP eval(); what remains is real eval(var_export()) in the config cache and an unguarded rm -rf in a release script

repos.name: cleanarchitecture
repos.why: C# + Angular + React — first contact 39 blocking, 26 of them SEO/a11y rules on the two SPA index.html shells; what remains is real: strict:false, a committed .env, unlabeled inputs, log-and-eat catches in a React component

repos.name: ktor
repos.why: Kotlin — first contact 21 blocking, 14 of them a test.html under test-resources/ scored as a public page, plus a Gradle compile failure in our environment reported as failing tests; what remains is six real TODO() stubs and one third-party workflow on @main

repos.name: vapor
repos.why: Swift — first contact 6 blocking: its own reusable workflows on @main and README section gaps; what remains is a *.key file the .gitignore does not cover

repos.name: nest
repos.why: TypeScript monorepo (npm workspaces) with an integration/ e2e tree and sample apps — first contact 39 blocking: a logger class told it uses console, tsconfig flags as build verdicts, mongodb://localhost fixtures as secrets, `.catch(() => {})` on a stored promise the caller awaits; what remains is six `reduce(async …)` in the e2e app, two npm-audit advisories and one committed PKCS#8 key

repos.name: trpc
repos.why: pnpm monorepo with members under examples/* and www — first contact 33 blocking: build configs and a CLI told they log to console, an OG-image generator scored as a web page, an Algolia search key as a secret, ternary env fallbacks as hardcoded URLs; what remains is four without alt, a real import cycle, a silent connect in a constructor and `${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}` in a shell; 2026-09-05 importCycle type-only elision: its one import cycle ran through two `import { type X }` edges — elided, never a cycle in emitted JS — ceiling ratchets down

repos.name: apollo-server
repos.why: npm-workspaces monorepo with a docs site — first contact 4 blocking: a CA bundle read as a private key, a README link the resolver could not follow, a destructured parameter the scope harvester missed; nothing remains

repos.name: prisma
repos.why: pnpm monorepo, packages/** nesting, a SQL toolkit that builds SQL by design — first contact 90 blocking: `${STORAGE_TABLE}` constants as injection, seeding loops in test/ as N+1, teardown catches as swallows, tsconfig/ and turbo.json as invalid JSON, `base.sha` as shell injection, an un-runnable test:integration as failing tests; what remains is DDL with a computed database name, three import cycles, telemetry catches and a dev-tool page without a description; 2026-09-05 importCycle type-only elision: the three import cycles it blocked on read their bindings in parameter defaults and method bodies — deferred, now a warning — ceiling ratchets down

repos.name: NodeGoat
repos.why: OWASP's deliberately vulnerable app — the recall floor
